newsitem.title: USA: Gateway 2000 ships 554,000 PCs in Q2.
newsitem.headline: Gateway 2000 ships 554,000 PCs in Q2.

text.p: Gateway 2000 Inc said Thursday it shipped 554,000 personal computers during the second quarter, a 31 percent increase over second quarter 1996 shipments of 424,000 units.

Gateway also reported second quarter revenue rose 23 percent over the same period last year to $1.39 billion from $1.14 billion of a year ago. Second quarter net income rose 10 percent to $56.5 million or $0.36 a share (adjusted for a two-for-one stock split on June 17, 1997) from $51.4 million or $0.33 in the second quarter of 1996.

"As we indicated last month, we anticipated that the quarter would come in like a lamb and go out like a lion and we built inventories and infrastructure accordingly," said Ted Waitt, Gateway 2000 chairman and CEO, in a statement. "Demand did not accelerate as fast as we thought until the end of the quarter, resulting in higher than desired inventory levels."

Gateway said it plans to work the inventory down to more favorable levels in the second half of the year and also efficiently utilize the infrastructure it has in place for the anticipated second half demand.
It said its investment in inventory increased over Q1.

Gateway said its investment in inventory increased $145 million over first quarter, primarily due to purchases expecting higher demand and strategic purchases of certain components in connection with second half sales initiatives.
As a result, inventory turns decreased to 11.9 turns, compared to 18.7 turns last year.
Gateway also said its gross profit margins in the quarter were 18.7 percent of revenues, up from 18.1 percent a year ago, and consistent with the levels of the first quarter.
Average unit price ($2,515) was down 6.3% from the relatively high level of the second quarter of 1996 ($2,683).
As a result, sales growth slowed compared with unit shipment growth.

Gateway said its European shipments increased 47 percent in the second quarter over the second quarter of 1996, and shipments in the Asia Pacific region were up 90 percent over the second quarter of 1996. International sales were 18 percent of total sales, about the same as in first quarter.

Unit shipments of portable products continued to accelerate and were up 112 percent compared to a year ago. Revenues from portables represented a historical high of 12.5 percent of total revenue in the quarter.
Gateway said selling, general and administrative (SG&A) expenses for the quarter increased 33 percent versus the second quarter last year.

Waitt added that Gateway's recent purchase of Advanced Logic Research Inc will help the company make more inroads into the corporate market, along with its new product line aimed specifically at the corporate market.

"We anticipate increasing our competitiveness in the corporate marketplace, which should accelerate our revenue growth in what we expect will be a very strong overall market in the second half of the year," Waitt said.
